fields.description:
Discovered during the DC<->Cloud test-parity re-audit (epic 3e73-72b5-cff2-40f0).

DC guards that status is NEVER edited as a field:
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_outbound_status_routing_5200.py::test_the_dc_transport_never_edits_status_as_a_field`.

Cloud has the correct implementation — `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`
`update_issue()` pops `status` out of kwargs and routes it to `transition_issue()`, and only the
remaining kwargs become `jira workitem edit --<field>` argv — but NO Cloud test pins it. A future
refactor could leave `status` in the edit payload (a partial fix Jira keeps rejecting) with every
existing Cloud test still green.

Scope: TEST-ONLY. Behaviour-preserving; no production file is modified. The new test drives the
real `acli.update_issue` with `acli.transition_issue` and `acli_subprocess._run_acli` stubbed
(deterministic, no subprocess, no network), mirroring the stubbing style of
`test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New file `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_cloud_outbound_status_routing_6194.py` exists and
      contains the Cloud parity guard, with a docstring naming the DC test it mirrors.
- [ ] A test asserts that `acli.update_issue("PROJ-1", status="in_progress", summary="s")` produces
      a `jira workitem edit` argv that contains `--summary` and does NOT contain `--status` (nor the
      string `status` as any flag), proving status never reaches the field set.
- [ ] A test asserts that same call dispatches exactly one `transition_issue(key, "in_progress")`,
      so the guard cannot be satisfied by simply dropping status on the floor.
- [ ] A test asserts that a status-ONLY update (`update_issue("PROJ-1", status="closed")`) spawns NO
      `workitem edit` subprocess at all and returns `{"key": "PROJ-1", "status": "closed"}`.
- [ ] No file under `src/` changes (verified: `git diff --stat` touches only `tests/`).

## Testing

- [ ] Proof: `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_cloud_outbound_status_routing_6194.py -q`
      passes.
- [ ] Proof: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass from the worktree venv.
- [ ] Proof: the guard is falsifiable — checked by temporarily re-adding `status` to the edit kwargs
      locally and confirming the new test FAILS, then reverting.
